roleTitle: I take a product from the first question to running in production.
paragraphs: I'm Pujan Bajracharya, an AI product engineer. I run Design Bakery as a one-person studio. I research the problem, design the screens, build the front end, back end and AI, deploy it on servers I run, and keep watching it after launch.

It all runs on infrastructure I built: Octo, a self-hosted data platform that gives every project its own database, files and search; a server that deploys straight from GitHub; and traces and evals on every agent. You get a working product, not a prototype that needs another team to finish it.

I also build the tools that let one person move this fast: a coordination pack so several coding agents can work on one repository, a video studio that agents can drive, and a lab that checks AI judges against real answer keys.

highlights.title: Live voice agents
highlights.desc: Agents people talk to on a website. They ask one thing at a time, confirm before they act, and never press Submit for you.

highlights.title: Answers from your documents
highlights.desc: Chat and search over your own files. Every answer shows where it came from, and it says so when your files don't cover the question.

highlights.title: A working demo in a week
highlights.desc: A short fixed-price sprint that puts a demo on your real data, one you can click or call, then gives you findings and a fixed price for the full build.

highlights.title: Built, deployed, watched
highlights.desc: The whole stack, from design to servers: web app, API, database, deploys from GitHub, and monitoring once it is live.

callout: You pay for an outcome at a fixed price, not for hours. Hiring? I fit forward-deployed and founding engineer roles: close to the customer, and responsible for the product end to end.
